- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- If model shows a sharp spike in forecast followed by a drop, it often overshoots; cap peak forecasts or add a downward bias after spike.
- Model frequently underreacts to sentiment shifts in early days of forecast horizon; apply a lagged sentiment multiplier (e.g., 0.8–0.9) to recent sentiment for longer-term forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is >10% above forecast, check if sentiment was bullish 3–5 days prior; if yes, model may have missed momentum; adjust upward by 2–5%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” swings, model tends to lag; apply a 1–2 day delay correction to price movements in forecast.
